answer.rationale: Primary contract expires in 14 days with no auto-renew; doing nothing risks delivery. memory_c4 documents that renegotiating at renewal recovered real margin by benchmarking market rates, moving the incumbent on price and payment terms. Negotiating a renewal with the incumbent directly addresses the 18% cut mandate while preserving delivery continuity (supported by memory_c1 showing incumbent renewal kept integration stable with no migration or delivery interruption). Deferring is not viable given the 14-day expiry and 94% line utilization. Switching primary vendor carries integration/onboarding risk that conflicts with the delivery-risk constraint at 94% utilization. Adding a second source does not resolve the imminent primary expiry. Negotiate_terms is the single action that simultaneously targets cost reduction and delivery stability.
